posts.headline: Americans are on track to borrow a record $21.3 billion just to get through the holidays.
posts.source: Source: Adobe Analytics; Retail Council of Canada x Leger, 2026
posts.caption:
Americans are on track to borrow a record $21.3 billion just to get through the holidays.

Adobe projects a record $275.1 billion in U.S. online holiday spending this year, up 6.7% — and $21.3 billion of it on 'buy now, pay later.' Miss a payment and the fees start, turning December gifts into January debt.

In Canada it's the reverse: 56% say inflation is reshaping their plans, and average spending is down $64 to $911 (Retail Council of Canada x Leger).

My take: a record sales number isn't a record good year — it can just mean more of it was borrowed.

Buy now, pay later this year, or cash?

Source: Adobe Analytics; Retail Council of Canada x Leger, 2026

#BlackFriday #HolidayShopping #BNPL #PersonalFinance

paragraphs: Adobe projects U.S. shoppers will put a record $21.3 billion on 'buy now, pay later' this season — inside a record $275.1 billion in online spending, up 6.7% from last year. (Adobe Analytics, Sept. 2026)
Buy now, pay later splits a purchase into four payments. Miss one and the fees and interest begin — which is how holiday gifts quietly become January debt.
In Canada it's the reverse: 56% of shoppers say inflation is reshaping their holiday plans, and average planned spending fell $64 to $911. (Retail Council of Canada x Leger, 2026)
My take: a record sales number isn't the same as a record good year — it can just mean more of it was borrowed.
Are you using buy now, pay later this holiday, or paying cash?
